cohort: The study included 260 pregnant women, categorized into lean (n=71), normal weight (n=75), overweight (n=56), and obese (n=58) groups based on BMI.
finding: Pregnant women with overweight and obesity exhibited reduced RIZ1 expression and activated AKT/mTOR pathways, alongside higher baby weights, increased cesarean section rates, and altered plasma carnitine and amino acid profiles.
mod_finding: Pregnant women with obesity had higher cesarean section rates compared to other BMI groups.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy, with birth outcomes recorded at delivery.
birth_weight: Varied, with higher baby weights observed in pregnant women with obesity.
